LESSON: GUIDED READING: EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.5 Guided Reading: Reading Aloud (2 Sessions) • Articulation • Verbal c
Topic 2.7: Guided Reading: Extensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Reading: Extensive Reading, part of Reading 2.5 Guided Reading: Reading Aloud (2 Sessions) • Articulation • Verbal c in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why is reading important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. select appropriate reading materials from digital and non-digital sources,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Reading: Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Reading: Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a reading log to monitor reading activities,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Reading: Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. recommend to peers appropriate reading materials for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Reading: Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. select appropriate reading materials from digital and non-digital sources,

   Guided Reading: Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning,

   Guided Reading: Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. create a reading log to monitor reading activities,

   Guided Reading: Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. recommend to peers appropriate reading materials for enjoyment.

   Guided Reading: Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to select reading materials from various digital and non-digital sources,

2. conduct a silent reading session to read the materials identified,

3. make notes on the events in the texts,

4. prepare a reading log on the texts read indicating key details e.g. author, title, characters, events and personal opinion on text,

5. engage in reading activities for pleasure and understanding with assistance from parents,

6. collaborate with peers to form a reading club for Arabic materials.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to select reading materials from various digital and non-digital sources,
2. conduct a silent reading session to read the materials identified,
3. make notes on the events in the texts,
4. prepare a reading log on the texts read indicating key details e.g. author, title, characters, events and personal opinion on text,
5. engage in reading activities for pleasure and understanding with assistance from parents,
6. collaborate with peers to form a reading club for Arabic materials.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Reading: Extensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: These are promoted as the learner contributes to group decision making when

collaborating with peers to form a reading club for Arabic materials.

• Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner plans and manages tasks effectively when preparing a reading log on the

texts read, indicating key details.

1. select appropriate reading materials from digital and non-digital sources,
2. read varied appropriate grade appropriate materials for lifelong learning,
3. create a reading log to monitor reading activities,
4. recommend to peers appropriate reading materials for enjoyment.
